execution_steps: 1. Pivoted from the prior tick's oracle-machinery fix (FF6-EVENT-000275) back to per-format obligation closure per the Stop hook's product-first reminder. 2. Confirmed build_space_transform was exported at package top-level but never called internally anywhere in src/python/nrrd/src/format_factory/nrrd/ except its own module and __init__.py's re-export -- grep-verified zero internal call sites before this change.

3. Confirmed both 'space directions' and 'space origin' are REQUIRED arguments to build_space_transform (it raises on either being None), so the wiring only invokes it when a document's header actually declares both -- space metadata is otherwise entirely optional per NRRD0004+ and must not become a mandatory check.

5. Added the wiring inside validate()'s existing try block, catching NrrdParseError specifically (matching the function's own established exception-to-diagnostic pattern) and appending a new 'nrrd.space.inconsistent' diagnostic code rather than letting the exception propagate.

6. Manually verified via a real header round-tripped through dumps/loads (not a hand-built NrrdDocument, which the existing test suite's own _document() helper pattern in test_obligation_axis_field_arity.py establishes as the correct construction path) that: consistent fields validate cleanly, an origin/directions length mismatch is reported, and no-space-fields documents are unaffected.

7.
